How do I calculate my caloric needs when accounting for hypothyroidism?

Study metabolism here. Why most web-based resources tell you you should consume 2000-2200 calories/day, the truth is that most people require far less. I'd recommend keeping meticulous records and trying 1400, 1600, and 1800 calories of intake/day for a week each. Things that never happen in Star Trek

The power surge on the bridge thing has always floored me. Not only have they apparently forgotten to fuse any circuit, but they have high-voltage running everywhere because they have forgotten how to use relays.

Apparently those exploding consoles are a very realistic problem

What you are seeing when a console explodes is the failure of the insulators and surge protectors. Just like the product I work with, Starfleet Issue Protective Isolators would have a maximum rating.

During combat, lets face it... both sides are slinging massive amounts of power around trying to make the opposing side explode. Eventually one or more isolators are going to be overwhelmed and an arc is going to jump between the power-carrying components of the ship and the frame... and all that power has to go somewhere.

Sometimes it dissipates harmlessly, other times it causes things to fail catastrophically. Frankly given the power levels we are talking about I'm surprised there aren't more internal explosions.

Source: http://scifi.stackexchange.com/questions/7511/why-do-consoles-explode-in-star-trek

The Fossil Fighters series. Brief summary: Raise dinosaurs back from the dead into a weird new virtual life. The better you clean the fossils the stronger your Vivosaur is. They can get stronger in battle, but cleaning their fossils is actually the fastest way to kicking ass.

Least favourite game play part: Those dark fossils that have a special hard casing that prevents you from using the x-ray to see what is inside and can only be opened by using your hammer tools. This could have been an interesting challenge, except for a few certain things:

  1. Many fossils are encased in the same shaped rocks so you can't rely on memory on where to best place your tools to not damage the hidden fossil inside.
  2. The rocks that hold the fossils are of different softness levels. Some fall apart using the weakest tools. Again, the only way to break this dark shell is using the hammer, the most powerful tool.
  3. There is no way to test the softness of what is underneath the special dark shell.
  4. The dark shell does not absorb the impact of the hammer. If you hit a soft fossil with a hammer directly kiss those bones goodbye because that shit is now dust.

Story: I love stories in my games. I will play a genre I wouldn't usually, or a mechanically bad game if I like the story enough. But hooooooly molly no one on staff of these games knows how to write a story. They grabbed all the necessary hero's journey bones to make the skeleton but never fleshed it out. The flattest/plain characters. Too much telling not showing. Games in general kind of need it for game play introduction's sake, but this was ridiculous. The writing felt very insecure of itself.
